rows.why: Rule 1: deg-4 hub at lowest z (38) is where both long tracks (to 19002 at z=250 and to 19018 at z=224) and the short heavy prongs ending orange/red near 19008/19012 all emanate from, i.e. everything gets hotter going away from it.

Rule 1/5: 16004 is the real 3-D kink where a ~110 cm MIP track meets a ~60 cm greener track that gets hotter toward its stopping end 16005, plus a stub, and it is the lower-z junction (rule 2); the alternative end 16003 (deg 4) is rejected because it sits on the y~200 top face, so its three stubs are boundary fragments of an exiting track.

Textbook rule 1: three prongs all get hotter going away from 13002 - two short yellow->dark-red protons to 13001/13003 and one long MIP muon that only reddens at its far end 13000; 13002 is also the lowest-z node.
Rule 1: the only long track cools toward the deg-4 stub cluster at 16004 (z=68, lowest z) and brightens to yellow/orange at its far end where it reaches the x=-200 boundary.

Both ends of the single 250 cm track carry an endpoint hot spot (trap 2), so I use prong multiplicity: 10002 is a deg-4 node with three ~10-15 cm prongs (hadronic vertex), while the rejected alternative 10001 is a bare deg-1 end sitting at y=194.5, i.e. on the top face where a track enters/exits.
Rule 1: at the deg-3 node 15002 a ~28 cm prong runs orange->dark red away to 15001 (stopping proton) and a long MIP track runs away to the x=-200 boundary; 15002 is also the lowest-z candidate.

Rule 1: the ~10 cm dark-red prong to 20001 starts at 20004 (lowest z, 188) and the long MIP track to the z=500 boundary starts there too - the 2-3 cm stubs 20009/20011 hanging off 20008/20010 read as delta rays along the first 12 cm of that muon, not as fragments of a 22 cm proton, which rules out the alternative reading with the vertex at 20010.
Rule 8: the whole cluster is a ~4 cm compact hot blob with no readable direction - all three candidates lie within 4 cm, so I take the central deg-2 node 19001 and claim no real discrimination.

Rule 1: 11076 is the apex of a clean V whose two arms each brighten monotonically away from it (yellow->dark red toward 11004, cyan->orange toward 11005), and it is the lowest-z candidate with the pi0-like shower activity opening downstream of it.
Rule 1/6: deg-3 node with a stub where a track brightening to orange at its far end 18000 meets a low-charge shower-like prong toward 18001; 18002 is the only junction in the cluster.

The only multi-prong node: 17002 (deg 3) carries two ~5 cm stubs, one ending dark red at 17000, while the alternative end 17001 is a bare deg-1 point sitting on the z=0 detector face where a track enters/exits - prong multiplicity beats the rule-2 low-z preference here.
Rule 1: the long track leaves the deg-3 node 5003 as cyan MIP and brightens to orange at its stopping end 5000, and 5003 carries two short stubs and is the lowest-z candidate.
Rule 8: the cluster is a compact blob and all four candidates lie within ~5 cm of each other, so the choice carries no information; I take the deg-3 node 20002.

Rule 1: 7010 is the deg-4 convergence at the lowest z (84) from which the long MIP track to the z=500 boundary, the prong toward 7006, and the 7012/7013/7011 chain all radiate; the ambiguity is that this cluster could be a cosmic with vertex-like debris at that hub.
Rule 8 abstention: a diffuse ~100 cm cloud of mostly grey (no-dQ/dx) dots with no track, apex or direction to read, so there is no evidence the candidate location is the interaction point at all.
Rule 1 two-Bragg-ends: a ~130 cm MIP track ends dark red at 14001 and a short ~13 cm orange/red stub ends at 14000; 14002 is the deg-2 junction both point away from.

Rule 1: the ~140 cm track ends orange (Bragg) at 8001, so the vertex is the other end; 8032 is the least-extreme (lowest-z) node of the 4-vertex knot there, i.e. where the long track meets the short dark-red stub running out to 8000.

Rule 1: a ~13 cm prong rises monotonically yellow-orange-dark red into 9004 (stopping proton) and a low-dQ/dx shower-like arm runs the other way to 9010; 9007 is the deg-2 junction they both leave from, and it is at lower z than 9004 (rule 2).
Rule 1 textbook: deg-3 hub with two short dark-red prongs (to 6001 and 6004, both stopping protons) and one MIP track to 6000 - every attached segment gets hotter going away from 6003.

Rule 8-ish: a single ~135 cm uniformly MIP track with no Bragg at either end; the only two candidates sit 2.8 cm apart at the low-z end, so I take the extreme tip 41010 but this is close to a coin flip between the two ids.
Rule 1: deg-3 hub where a ~145 cm muon (Bragg dark red at its far end 13000) meets a ~6 cm dark-red proton prong to 13001 and a short cool prong to 13016 - all three heat up away from 13015.

Rule 1: deg-3 hub at low z (19.7 cm) with three prongs, two of which end in clear Bragg peaks (dark red at 16013 and at 16009) and one long green prong to 16000; 16004 3.7 cm away is the hot tip of a stub, not the junction.
Rule 1: deg-5 hub whose own dQ/dx is green (MIP-level) with several dark-red prongs radiating outward, the longest ending dark red at 23000 - every attached segment gets hotter away from 23002.
Rule 1: a ~4 cm dark-red stub ends at 12002 (stopping proton) and a ~24 cm cyan/green MIP track runs to 12000; 12001 is the deg-2 junction and is at lower z than 12002 (rule 2).

Rules 1+7: a heavy backward track ends dark red at 11001 and a diffuse EM spray opens forward to z~250, so the vertex is at the heavy track's forward (cool) attachment, the deg-2 node 11017 at z=125; the 15 other candidates in the z=138-166 tangle are plausible alternatives I cannot separate from the projections alone.
Rule 1: the only visible ~11 cm segment rises to a dark-red Bragg end at 9001, so the vertex is the cool end, and 9000 is the deg-3 node of the three co-located candidates there.

Rule 8: essentially an empty event - a 3.5 cm two-point stub plus unmeasured grey dots; the only readable direction is yellow at 3001 rising to dark red at 3000, so I take the cool end 3001 (also lower z), but this is near-guessing.

Rule 1: the ~205 cm track warms to green/orange at its low end (15000/15006/15007) and is cool cyan at the high end, so the vertex is the deg-3 node 15008 at the cool, lower-z end where a short green prong to 15001 also attaches.

Rule 1: the ~185 cm muon rises green-yellow-dark red into 13001 (clear stopping end), so the vertex is the far end; along that far end the chain runs 13000 (green, coolest point in the event) -> 13002 (orange) -> ... -> 13001 (dark red), so the segment heats monotonically away from 13000 and 13000 is the vertex.

Rule 8: the cluster is a ~7 cm blob of three vertices surrounded by disconnected grey (no-dQ/dx) fragments with no readable prong direction; the deg-2 node 53030 is the hot one, which contradicts placing the vertex there, so I abstain rather than invent a reason.

Rule 1: the deg-3 junction at the lowest-z end of the cluster, with a short dark-red stub running away from it to 84095 and a MIP-level track running away up-right toward 84096; both attached prongs get hotter away from it.

Rule 1 + rule 2: the only junction (deg 2) and the lowest-z point; a very hot short stub ends at 12001 and a longer MIP track leaves it and rises to orange only at its far end 12000, so both prongs stop away from 12002.

Rule 1 on the one readable prong: the long track that ends dark red at 12013 must start at the blob, and it attaches at the low-y/low-z corner of the blob where the highest-degree vertex (deg 5) sits, which is also the apex of the activity that opens toward +z; the blob itself is too dense to check every segment.

Rule 1: single long track, monotone yellow-orange-red rise over the last ~20 cm into 12000 (a Bragg stop), track is cool cyan approaching 12001, so 12001 is the start end; rule 2 agrees (z=185 vs 294).
Rule 2 + topology: the deg-3 junction in the tight knot of short stubs at the low-z end (z~1-6 cm) from which the single long MIP track runs away to 13000 at z=300 with no Bragg rise at the knot end.

Rule 1 + rule 2: deg-2 junction at the lowest z, with a short hot (red) stub ending at 18001 and a cool green MIP track running away to 18000 at the x=201 anode edge, so the hot end is the stub's stopping point, not the vertex.
Rule 8: the whole object is a ~5 cm all-dark-red blob with no readable direction and no separable prongs, so any click is as good as another and I abstain rather than invent a reason.

Rule 1 in its clean form: deg-3 junction at the lowest z with a short uniformly dark-red proton stub stopping at 15003 and a cool cyan/green MIP track leaving toward 15000 at the anode edge; every attached segment gets hotter going away.
Rule 1 + rule 2: deg-2 junction at the lowest z, short dark-red stub to 11002 and a ~90 cm track that stays cyan leaving it and rises to yellow/orange only at its far end 11000.

Rule 1 by elimination: this cluster is a single straight ~85 cm track (9001-9002-9000) that warms toward 9000 at the x=201 anode edge, so 9001 is the cooler end; the dark-red Bragg end further up-left is a different cluster (candidate lists elsewhere in this worklist are complete per cluster while the panels draw all clusters), and no candidate here looks like a genuine multi-prong vertex.

Rule 1 on the one clean prong: the dark-red track rises monotonically toward its low-z end near 8001/8017, so that end is a Bragg stop and the vertex is at its cool end, which terminates at the deg-3 junction 8009 where the dense shower-like activity begins; the z=140-200 blob holds several competing deg-3 junctions (8037, 8007) I cannot separate from this rendering.
Rule 7: the cluster is a shower-like object that is narrow at z~155 and fans out (y from -122 to -137) by z~235, so the apex is the low-z end, where the deg-4 vertex 11005 sits; rule 2 agrees.
Rule 2 + topology: the long track runs from the deg-2 junction 19001 in mid-detector down to 19000 at the y=-199 bottom edge (an exit, not a stop), and 19001 is the lower-z, non-boundary end.

Rule 1: a single curved track with a textbook monotone rise (green-yellow-orange-dark red) over its last ~20 cm into 7001/7002, so that end is the Bragg stop and the cool 7000 end is the start; only the end is certain, not that the neutrino vertex lies on this single-track object at all (rule 5).
Rule 1 + rule 2: the track leaves the deg-2 junction 14003 cool and rises to orange/red at its far end 14000 (z=496), with a short hot stub to 14001 at the junction; 14003 is the lowest-z candidate.

Rule 1: a ~7 cm dark-red (Bragg) stub runs 16002->16001 and the ~230 cm MIP track leaves 16002 the other way rising only to orange at 16000, so both prongs get hotter away from the 16002 junction; rule 2 also favours this low-z end (z=249 vs 460).
Featureless ~46 cm MIP track with no Bragg at either end; the 15000 end is marginally hotter (green vs teal) and rule 2 favours the lower-z end, so 15001 by weak tie-break only.

A ~180 cm straight MIP track with no Bragg anywhere (cosmic-like); 13000 sits on the y=-198 bottom wall so it is an exiting end, leaving the contained low-z end 13001 (rule 2) as the only plausible vertex.
Rule 1: the ~185 cm MIP track terminates at 8004 and a ~11 cm stub rises monotonically orange->dark red away from it to a Bragg peak at 8006, so both attached objects point away from 8004.
Rule 1 in its clean form: three prongs (to 16001, 16005, 16000) all leave the degree-3 node 16004 as green/cyan and all rise to orange/dark red at their far ends.

Rule 1 + rule 3: a ~7 cm dark-red proton stub runs 15004->15001, while the ~110 cm muon leaves 15004 as cyan, Braggs to red at 15003 and has a cool short segment (Michel-like) hanging off that far end, so 15003 is the stopping end and 15004 the vertex.

Rule 1: the ~160 cm track rises monotonically green->orange->dark red into a textbook Bragg stop at 15003, so the vertex is the far end, where a short heavily-ionising 3 cm stub (15004->15002->15000) hangs off the MIP track.

A ~370 cm straight MIP track that exits at the x=-201 wall (17000), so 17001 is the only candidate that can be a vertex; but its single hot end point (not a monotonic rise, trap 2) reads more like a stopping cosmic than a neutrino vertex.

Rule 1 with a sharp kink: at 9002 the ~120 cm MIP arm heads off to the z=500 wall (no Bragg, exiting) while the other arm turns orange immediately and rises to a dark-red Bragg stop at 9001 - a proton and a muon both pointing away.
Trap 1 resolved: both far ends heat up (dark-red Bragg at 13000, orange rise at 13001) and the two arms meet at a ~90 degree kink at 13002, which is also the lowest-z point (rule 2).

Rule 8 case - the cluster is a ~2 cm blob of a few very hot points with no readable direction and the rest of the event is isolated dots; all three candidates coincide within 2.5 cm so I name the degree-2 middle node, but this is close to a guess.

Dense ~40 cm blob with 14 candidates and no clean prong structure; the object is compact and dark red at its upstream (low-z) tip and thins into a green spray toward +z, so by rules 7 and 2 I take the apex node 8001, where a ~13 cm heavily-ionising stub (to 8010) attaches to the rest.
Rule 1: the single ~40 cm track rises monotonically yellow->orange->dark red into a Bragg stop at 17000, so the vertex is the cool low-z end 17003 (a lone stopping proton, no second prong visible).

The only vertex-like feature is the two-prong MIP junction at 19001 (a ~78 cm arm and a ~30 cm arm), and rule 2 favours it, but it sits in the detector corner (y=198, z=0) so this reads much more like a cosmic entry point than a neutrino vertex.

Rules 7+1: the whole dense object starts at z~202 and opens out toward +z, and at the degree-3 apex node 11002 a short dark-red stub leaves to a Bragg tip at 11009 while the heavy backbone leaves the other way into the shower.
